answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock stake in a shared registry before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. The registry’s kernel records deposits and links each identity to its own locked funds; when a verified task dispute proves fraud, the protocol slashes that stake and distributes part to the challenger. Spawning a sybil farm therefore requires capital for every identity, and coordinated fraud risks losing it. The garden of agents stays open to newcomers, while an atlas of identities alone grants no economic power.
